name: In-app browser
note: Browser pane built into the agent's desktop app
summary: The agent's desktop app ships its own browser pane, with sign-ins and cookies kept apart from the user's everyday browser. The agent opens pages, reads them, clicks, types and fills in forms there while the user watches in the app. It is the reverse of an agentic browser: the agent vendor builds a browser into the agent app, rather than the browser vendor building an assistant into the browser. When the session runs in the cloud, the desktop app relays the actions, so it has to stay open.
how: The user opens the browser pane next to the session in the desktop app
The user signs in, inside the pane, to the sites the agent should use
The agent opens, reads and acts on pages, asking before it acts on a new site
Pages load from the user's device, so cloud sessions need the app open and online
facts: Kept in the app's own browser storage, not the user's browser
Nothing to install and logins are kept apart from the user's own browser, but it is tied to the desktop app being open
goodFor: Web tasks without handing over the user's everyday logins
Watching and taking over in the same app
Checking a local web app next to the agent's session
watchOut: Every page the agent reads can carry a prompt injection
Needs the desktop app open and online
Sites that need the user's identity need a fresh sign-in in the pane
